Freescale magnetic calibration (magcal.c, matrix.c), via PJRC MotionCal
=======================================================================

License:    BSD-3-Clause
Used in:    qtcalibrate
Source:     https://github.com/PaulStoffregen/MotionCal
Upstream:   Freescale Sensor Fusion Library, magnetic.c and matrix.c,
            copyright 2014, 2015; succeeded by the NXP ISSDK sensor fusion
            library, which carries the same BSD-3-Clause grant with an SPDX
            tag and reworks the solvers into incremental slices.

What PJRC changed, measured against the unmodified upstream on 2026-10-10:

  matrix.c   Token for token the same, bar renames (eigencompute10 ->
             eigencompute), fabsf -> fabs in the eigensolver and the pivot
             search, dropped trailing `return;` statements, and a write-only
             singular-matrix flag removed from fmatrixAeqInvA's signature --
             upstream declares and passes it but never reads it. Two guards
             against multiplying a zero element are gone from the Gauss-Jordan
             inner loops; those are a speed shortcut upstream, not a result.
             f3x3matrixAeqB and the 4x4 eigensolver are absent, and this
             solver calls neither.

  magcal.c   The arithmetic is upstream's, line for line. What differs is
             where the samples come from: upstream's three solvers each walk a
             14x28 direction-binned mesh held in a separate MagneticBuffer and
             scale by a sensor struct's counts-per-uT, while these read a flat
             650-sample array folded into the calibration struct itself, with
             counts-per-uT fixed at 1. That is why upstream's magnetic.h does
             not declare these functions and could not be adopted in place of
             the header here: its buffer is also its sample retention policy,
             and qtcalibrate has its own.

  The coupling is shallow, though. Upstream's magnetic.c is these three
  solvers plus four functions qtcalibrate implements elsewhere: an
  initialiser, a scheduler deciding which solver runs and how often
  (MagCal_Run here), an apply step that is invW * (B - V) and lives in
  CompassCalibration, and the mesh buffer updater. The solvers take the buffer
  as a parameter and touch it only to iterate, so the per-solver difference is
  about twenty lines of sample walk each.

This file's notice is the one both copies carry.
